hints.title: Mirror Reflection Obstacle
hints.text: A tree is symmetric if it is a mirror image of itself around the root. How can a helper function compare mirror branches (left against right) rather than identical branches?

hints.title: Mirror Subtree Invariant
hints.text: Mirror symmetry requires the left subtree's left child to match the right subtree's right child, and the left subtree's right child to match the right subtree's left child.

hints.title: Dual-Pointer Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Define a helper taking two nodes. If both are null, return true. If one is null or values differ, return false. Recursively check helper(t1.left, t2.right) and helper(t1.right, t2.left). Call helper on root.left and root.right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (1 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Linear traversal visiting each node at most once with recursion stack depth bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: In-order traversal alone does not uniquely identify symmetric trees without storing null leaf pointers.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Cross-pairing left.left with right.right and left.right with right.left.
